prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Hi, I am looking for a white wine from Chile that is a little sweet and light, with some spice flavors."

List A:
Wine 1: White Blend, Italy, $10. Tasting note: "Described as medium-sweet on the label, this light white wine offers tones of peach nectar, honey and white flower. It is a simple and one dimensional wine with a subtle touch of sweetness on the close. Pair it with salty appetizers."
Wine 2: Chardonnay, Italy, $38. Tasting note: "Here is a quintessentially luminous and fragrant white wine from southern Italy (made with 100% Chardonnay, two thirds of which was aged in oak) that delivers food-friendly appeal, succulence and a sophisticated approach. The wine is thick and luscious on the palate and offers slightly sweet flavors of exotic fruit, mango and papaya."
Wine 3: Riesling, US, $9. Tasting note: "If you like your white wines fruity and sweet, this one's for you. It has pretty flavors of peaches, honey and spices."
Wine 4: Red Blend, Chile, $10. Tasting note: "This wine, like so many from the 1998 vintage in Chile, is very light in texture and displays little depth. The flavors are accurate for a claret—mild berry and a touch of earth—and there's even a decent finish. A light quaff; don't expect weight."
Wine 5: Sauvignon Blanc, France, $30. Tasting note: "This wine is soft, although with plenty of ripe fruit. It has a touch of spice and light acidity, showing the richness of the white-wine vintage. Drink now."

List B:
Wine 1: Sauvignon Blanc, Chile, $11. Tasting note: "Light, lucid and exactly what we're looking for from Chile. This organic wine has pure varietal aromas of nettles, tarragon and citrus, which are followed by flavors of green fruits, scallion and pepper. It's super zesty and spritzy, with a cleansing finish. About as true as they come in this price range."
Wine 2: Fiano, US, $26. Tasting note: "This is an interesting, dry white wine from an unusual grape variety. It's more savory than fruity, as the aromas resemble white and black pepper, while flavors are subtle and figgy. The texture is quite rich and the finish lingers nicely. It's very full-bodied for a white, and definitely worth a try."
Wine 3: Gewürztraminer, US, $16. Tasting note: "I like this wine mainly for its dryness and crispness. It tastes balanced and wholesome, the way a white wine should be. It's not a heavy-hitter, but pleases for its spicy fruit, toffee and floral flavors."
Wine 4: Pinot Grigio, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a sweet, softly simple wine whose apricot, citrus and peach flavors will satisfy those looking for a decent everyday white wine."
Wine 5: Pinot Grigio, US, $12. Tasting note: "This wine has a personality that's both crisp and satisfying. White pepper and light earth aromas lead to tempting peachy flavors and an appealing texture that balances tanginess and richness. The blend includes small portions of Chardonnay, Albariño, Gewürztraminer and Orange Muscat."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
